item.title: PRINCETON SALES TAX PASSES
item.description: Residents of Princeton, or at least the few registered voters that voted in yesterday’s election, have overwhelmingly approved a half cent sales tax for the city. Franklin County Clerk, Janet Paddock, reports that only 20 people cast ballots in the election, for a 10% turnout rate. The tax will take effect July 1st. item.title: CARNEGIE GIFTS OTTAWA LIBRARY
item.description: The Ottawa Library has received a $10,000 gift from the Carnegie Corporation. Carnegie is gifting $10,000 to the 1,350 surviving Carnegie Libraries in the United States in celebration of the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence. Andrew Carnegie discovered the importance of libraries when a retired colonel opened his personal library to young factory workers in Pittsburgh. item.title: LEGISLATURE HEARS PROP TAX BILL
item.description: A bill that would limit local government property tax increases to 3% per year received its first Senate committee hearing yesterday, after clearing the Kansas House. The Senate Tax Committee reviewed the measure, which would exempt schools from the cap. If a city or county seeks to exceed the 3% limit, it could still pass its budget, but residents would have 30 days to collect signatures from 5% of registered voters to block the increase through a protest petition. item.title: MICO SIRENS
item.description: This week is Kansas Severe Weather Awareness Week. Miami County Emergency Management Coordinator, Mike Fleming, says Miami County has 15 storm sirens, but remember, sirens are designed to be heard outdoors and not necessarily indoors. The county can set off four storm sirens in the city limits of Louisburg. The City of Paola has nine storm sirens and Osawatomie has four and those cities control their own sirens. item.title: Duane Falley
item.description: Duane Daniel Falley, 63, of Victoria, KS died Saturday, February 14, 2026 at Melvern, Kansas at his farm where he and his wife Lynda planned to retire. He was born February 22, 1963 in Quinter, KS the son of Warren and Patricia (Younger) Falley. He received a Lucky High School diploma and graduated from Manhattan Area Technical College with a welding degree. He would then move to Victoria, KS in 1998. item.title: Clarence D McIlvain
item.description: Clarence D. McIlvain, age 84, of Ottawa, Kansas, passed away on March 3, 2026, at The University of Kansas Health System-Olathe in Olathe, Kansas. Born on October 9, 1941, in Madison, Kansas, Clarence was the beloved son of Robert Earl and Mary Elizabeth (Lewis) McIlvain.
